title: Docebo vs. Eightfold AI: enterprise skills and learning platform comparison
summary: Compare Docebo and Eightfold AI on skills intelligence, learning, recruiting, internal mobility, implementation, and pricing to find the right fit.
body_markdown:
Choosing between Docebo and Eightfold AI comes down to where your priority sits: do you need to execute learning and workforce strategy against validated skills data, or do you need agentic talent intelligence to drive talent acquisition and management?


Both are enterprise-grade platforms. They overlap on skills intelligence and internal mobility, but they lead with different problems.


- **Docebo** is a dual learning and skills platform (an[enterprise LMS](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/enterprise-learning-management/) paired with validated talent intelligence through[365Talents, a Docebo company](https://www.docebo.com/365talents) ) that closes the loop from skill-gap detection to learning delivery and internal mobility.
- **Eightfold AI** is an agentic talent intelligence platform for talent acquisition and talent management, with strengths in sourcing, candidate matching, internal talent matching, and employee career tools.


On the Docebo side, advanced skills intelligence means 365Talents, which you buy separately from Docebo’s LMS packages. It isn’t bundled into Elevate or Enterprise. Understand that relationship before you weigh any feature.


This guide compares the two on skills data, learning execution, career development, integrations, deployment, and pricing.


## **Docebo vs. Eightfold AI at a glance**


Here’s the fast version: Docebo with 365Talents fits when you need trusted skills data connected to learning delivery and internal mobility in one workflow. Eightfold AI fits when external hiring, sourcing, and candidate matching lead the purchase. The table below scores both across the eleven criteria enterprise buyers weigh most, where Advantage means fit for the stated requirement, not a tested benchmark.


**Evaluation criteria** **Docebo** **Eightfold AI** **Advantage** ****


**Core offering** Enterprise LMS plus skills intelligence via 365Talents Talent intelligence for acquisition and management Depends on mandate


**External recruiting** Not the focus Sourcing, CRM, candidate matching Eightfold


**Skills intelligence** 365Talents: inferred, governed, validated Skills recognized from profiles, work history, and other signals using AI, including deep learning Docebo for validated workforce intelligence


**Job architecture** 365Talents: governed roles, skills, proficiency Skills and role intelligence Docebo for governed internal architecture


**Internal mobility** 365Talents: matching, career paths Career Hub, internal matching Both, compare workflows


**Career development** 365Talents: skill-based paths Career Hub, development recommendations Docebo connects development directly to the internal skills picture


**Learning delivery** Docebo LMS delivers, tracks, certifies Recommends, runs elsewhere Docebo


**Compliance and extended enterprise** Docebo LMS: recurrence, certification, partners Not an LMS Docebo


**AI governance** ISO/IEC 42001 (365Talents, Feb 2025) ISO/IEC 42001 (Aug 14, 2025) Both, compare scope


**Deployment and support** LMS plus 365Talents, existing HRIS retained Talent products alongside your systems Depends on mandate


**Pricing and total cost** Separate LMS and 365Talents subscriptions Selected talent products Model your own TCO


## **When Docebo is the better fit**


Docebo’s approach to skills is to give you a continuously updated, AI-powered view of the skills across your organization, so you can identify capability gaps, anticipate workforce needs, and make smarter decisions about talent, learning, and mobility. Docebo is the better fit in these situations.


**Your skills initiative has to lead to training delivery.** Your skills initiative has to lead to learning. That connection is what sets 365Talents + Docebo apart. 365Talents identifies skills, gaps and development needs; Docebo delivers the learning to address them. Learning activity feeds back into the employee’s skills picture, creating a tighter loop between what the organization needs, what an employee needs to develop, and the learning they receive.


Because 365Talents is now part of Docebo, customers who use both can connect skills intelligence and learning within the same product ecosystem rather than integrating two unrelated vendors.


**You need a governed view of internal capability.** Skills data usually sits scattered across employee profiles, role definitions, project histories, and learning records. 365Talents pulls those signals into one governed picture, with standardized job architecture, proficiency levels, and validation rules. That gives HR, talent, and learning teams a consistent view instead of conflicting spreadsheets. When definitions are governed and comparable, workforce planning and internal mobility rest on the same source of truth.


**You want career development to give employees a reason to stay.** Retention improves when people can see where they can go next and how to get there. Docebo with 365Talents maps each employee’s validated skills to skill-based career paths and open roles, and Docebo delivers the learning that closes the gap between where they are and where they want to be. Employees get more than a promise of growth. They get a concrete path, with the training attached.


**You want to reduce external hiring costs.** Before paying recruiters and staffing agencies to find outside candidates, identify the employees who already have adjacent skillsets and upskill them into the new role. 365Talents surfaces those matches, and Docebo delivers the training that makes the move credible. Filling roles from within can lower recruiting spend and shorten time to productivity.


## **When Eightfold AI is the better fit**


**External hiring is the primary business problem.** Eightfold’s recruiting depth is real. If sourcing, candidate matching, CRM, and recruiter workflows are what you’re buying for, that’s where the platform concentrates its strength. A skills intelligence and learning pairing isn’t built to lead that job, so weigh Eightfold seriously when acquisition is the headline requirement rather than an afterthought.


**Recruiting and internal talent decisions share one mandate.** Eightfold spans the talent lifecycle, so a single mandate covering external hiring plus internal movement may suit its scope. Compare the exact products you’d be quoted, since the platform is modular. Confirm which capabilities are included in your configuration rather than assuming the full suite ships as one package.


**Your existing Eightfold investment already works.** If Eightfold is deployed and delivering on recruiting, coexistence is a fair option. You can evaluate whether to extend Eightfold into more talent workflows or to add dedicated skills and learning products alongside it. The question is which path gives you a stronger development-to-delivery loop, not whether you must choose one vendor for everything.


**You want to assess employee career tools alongside matching.** Eightfold Career Hub is an employee-facing development experience, and it references Eightfold Digital Twin work signals and development recommendations. If that’s on your evaluation list, test it on the same career and mobility scenario you give 365Talents. Judge both on how an employee moves from a gap to a credible next step.


## **Docebo vs. Eightfold AI detailed capability breakdown**


Docebo and Eightfold AI solve overlapping problems with different architectures, so a fair comparison looks at each capability on its own. Use this breakdown to score them where their jobs overlap and to see clearly where they don’t.


### **Core architecture and product scope**


Decide what you’re comparing before you compare anything.


- **Docebo LMS** delivers and tracks learning. **365Talents** **by Docebo** supplies[skills intelligence](https://www.docebo.com/learning-network/blog/skills-intelligence-platforms/) and internal mobility, and it can run standalone alongside an LMS you already own.
- **Eightfold** is a talent intelligence platform spanning talent acquisition and talent management, and it isn’t an LMS.


Those are three different jobs. Line up an entire vendor portfolio against a single product and you’ll draw the wrong conclusion. Match capability to capability instead. Ask each vendor which product does what, which system stores records, and where one tool hands off to the next. Then evaluate each product on the outcome it owns, not the logo above it. **Compare like for like, product to product, before you score any vendor.**


### **Skills data collection, inference, and validation**


The decision here is whether skills data reflects real work or just activity.


- **Docebo** infers skills from employee profiles, job histories, learning activity, projects, and manager input, then normalizes and updates them continuously. A course completion is one signal, not proof of proficiency.
- **Eightfold** infers from career and internal work signals too, so an “external data only” claim doesn’t hold up.


Both descriptions are vendor-stated, so treat them as starting points, not verdicts. Run each engine against your own people and watch how it handles edge cases, stale records, and conflicting inputs. The test is provenance, refresh cadence, correction rights, and manager approval. Check who can correct a wrong skill, how fast a change propagates, and whether a manager signs off before the data drives a decision.


### **Skills taxonomy and job architecture**


Your skills data is only as useful as the structure underneath it.


- **Docebo** governs role and skill definitions, proficiency levels, and normalization, so the same skill means the same thing across regions and functions.
- **Eightfold** brings its own skills and role intelligence, and it can work with internal frameworks you already maintain.


The difference shows up in messy data. Titles drift, teams invent their own labels, and acquired business units arrive with conflicting frameworks. So bring your messiest job titles and watch each vendor map and correct them live. Use real examples, not a tidy sample set, and see how the taxonomy holds when the inputs fight each other. A framework that only works on clean data won’t survive your org chart.


### **Internal mobility, career pathing, and employee experience**


Both vendors belong in a mobility evaluation, so judge them on what employees do, not what the demo promises.


- **Docebo** offers skill-based career paths, employee participation, and opportunity matching through an internal talent marketplace.
- **Eightfold** counts its Career Hub and internal matching among its strengths.


Ease of use decides whether either one gets adopted, because employees won’t return to a tool that buries the next step. Look past the polished screens and ask how people discover roles, express interest, and get matched to real openings. Then separate two numbers that often get blended: how many employees log in, and how many complete an internal move. Logins measure curiosity. **Completed moves measure impact, and one doesn’t prove the other.**


### **Learning execution and skill development**


This is where the two platforms play different roles.


- **Docebo** identifies skills and needs and delivers the learning and records completion and certification, covering corporate training, content management, and instructor-led training (ILT).
- **Eightfold** earns credit for its development recommendations, but recommending a course isn’t the same as running it.


Here’s an illustrative workflow. A gap gets detected, a course is assigned, it’s delivered in the LMS, and a readiness review confirms the skill. Treat that sequence as illustrative, not a guaranteed outcome. The real test is the handoffs, so ask each vendor to complete the gap-to-learning-to-readiness loop end to end. A recommendation that never reaches a delivery engine leaves the gap open, and a completion that never gets validated tells you nothing about capability.


### **Compliance training and extended enterprise learning**


Compliance is where the system of record matters most.


- **Docebo** handles compliance tracking, recurring certifications, and extended enterprise portals for customers and partners, and it supports[SCORM](https://help.docebo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360020128479-Uploading-and-managing-SCORM-as-training-material) ,[xAPI](https://help.docebo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360020128459-Uploading-xAPI-formerly-Tin-Can-API-content) , and[AICC](https://help.docebo.com/hc/en-us/articles/360020083220-Uploading-and-managing-AICC-training-material) per the Docebo Help Center.
- **Eightfold** isn’t an LMS, so the obvious question is which system runs and records the content when an auditor asks.


Don’t assume a talent platform closes that gap, because compliance failures carry real regulatory cost. Ask exactly where completions live, how recurring certifications reset, and how external audiences get controlled access. Then confirm the delivery engine and content-standard support directly with each vendor, because a missing standard means rebuilt content and a slower rollout.


### **Artificial intelligence and workforce readiness**


Judge AI by the tasks it performs, the data it uses, and the human controls around it.


- **Docebo** offers the Prism AI Agent, which matches talent with open positions to improve matching quality. Docebo also provides AI services on demand, including Job Architecture Audit, Skills Mapping & Skills Definition, and Skills Framework Enrichment.
- **Eightfold** surfaces Workforce Readiness metrics such as AI Potential and AI Adoption on its product page.


Those are workforce signals about where AI shows up in your organization, not measures of individual proficiency, so don’t read them as skill scores. Push past the feature names. Ask what each capability decides, what data feeds it, and where a person reviews or overrides the output before it affects someone’s career. **What to insist on: one demonstrated workflow with human review in the loop.**


### **AI governance and data controls**


Governance claims need scoping before they mean anything. Both vendors hold[ISO/IEC 42001](https://www.iso.org/standard/42001) .


- **Docebo** was[certified in February 2025](https://365talents.com/en/resources/365talents-becomes-world-first-hrtech-certified-iso42001/) as, in its words, the world’s first HR Tech provider certified for responsible AI.
- **Eightfold**[announced certification on August 14, 2025](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/08/14/3133748/0/en/Eightfold-AI-Achieves-All-Three-Levels-of-ISO-IEC-42001-2023-Certification.html) , claiming a first as a developer, provider, and consumer of third-party AI.


The scopes differ, and both are real. A certificate tells you a management system exists, not how it maps to your requirements. Walk each vendor through human oversight, data access, retention, hosting, and auditability against your own risk review. Match each control to that review, get the specifics in writing before you sign, and skip any EU AI Act legal conclusions.


### **HCM ecosystem and integrations**


Integrations decide whether skills data flows or stalls.


- **Docebo** lists[more than 100 pre-built connectors](https://365talents.com/en/use-case-integrate-for-a-seamless-experience/) covering HRIS, LMS, LXP, ATS, and BI, with named systems including Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, Oracle, Cornerstone, and ADP. That’s a different footprint from **Docebo LMS** integrations, which cover tools like Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and LinkedIn Learning.
- **Eightfold** functions as an AI talent intelligence layer that integrates with major systems like Workday and SAP SuccessFactors to enhance them rather than replace them.


Connector counts look impressive on a slide, so make each vendor prove it. Include SSO (single sign-on) in the test, since employees won’t adopt a tool with a clumsy login. Then watch a live data flow, break a sync on purpose, and require a named owner for the fix. **The test: a live data-flow demo, a failed sync, and someone accountable for it.**


### **Reporting and workforce outcomes**


Training activity and workforce readiness answer different questions, so match the report to the decision.


- **Docebo** reports completions, reports skills coverage, gaps, readiness, and mobility measures.
- **Eightfold** reports on recruiting, matching, and workforce priorities. A recurring reviewer critique is that Eightfold analytics stay at summary-dashboard level.


Take a compact example: validated skill progression, internal fill rate, time to internal placement, and hiring or contractor spend. Some of those figures need your own data or joined reporting across systems, so don’t assume they arrive as out-of-the-box dashboards. Agree on baseline, population, measurement period, and attribution before anyone discusses ROI. A metric without a baseline is a number you can’t defend.


### **Implementation, onboarding, and adoption**


Time to value depends on the use case, the data connections, and the adoption plan, not a vendor’s headline number.


- For **Docebo** with **365Talents** , scope role-framework work, integration, content mapping, pilot users, validation, and employee communications.
- For **Eightfold** , scope recruiting and talent workflows, data readiness, integrations, and user adoption.


[Alstom](https://365talents.com/en/resources/case_studies/alstom-builds-a-global-skills-intelligence-platform-with-365talents/) reached its milestones in roughly a nine-month window, which is one observation, not a standard promise, and 365Talents still needs data preparation like any skills platform. Treat every timeline as a hypothesis until a vendor commits to it. Ask for a phased plan with named data owners, acceptance criteria, and pilot outcomes, then hold them to the criteria you both signed.


### **Customer support and vendor accountability**


When an issue crosses the skills product, the learning system, and the integration, you need to know who owns the fix.


- For **Docebo** , confirm support and escalation ownership for **Docebo LMS** and **365Talents** . 365Talents is sold, contracted, and supported independently, so shared branding doesn’t prove one support agreement.
- For **Eightfold** , get support channels, coverage hours, and escalation terms for the exact products you’re quoted.


Assumptions fall apart the first time a ticket bounces between teams. So put the accountability in the contract rather than assuming vendor-led implementation. Name the escalation path, and confirm who your team calls at 2:00am when a sync fails and a launch is at risk.


### **Pricing and total cost of ownership**


Useful pricing covers the products and the operating costs to deliver the same outcome, not a single line item. None of these vendors publishes public pricing, so treat any number you hear as quote-specific.


- **Docebo** offers separate packages for learning and for skills intelligence.
- On the **Eightfold** side, expect selected talent products, implementation, integrations, and any learning system you keep.


Build the full picture before you compare, because the biggest costs often hide in services and administration. A combined learning-and-skills mandate may fit Docebo well, but that’s a fit judgment about your goals, not a claim that it costs less. Build a three-year TCO model covering subscriptions, implementation, integration, content and services, administration, and renewal.


### **Customer evidence**


Reviews are most useful when they describe the exact product and workflow a buyer plans to purchase. An LMS review doesn’t establish 365Talents skills quality, and an Eightfold recruiting review says little about employee development, so the Docebo side and Eightfold read best on their own terms.


On the learning side, **Docebo LMS** earns[4.3 out of 5 across 749 G2 reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/docebo/reviews) and[4.4 out of 5 across 242 Capterra reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/127213/Docebo/reviews/) (verified September 2026). The skills layer scores higher. **365Talents** holds[4.8 out of 5 across 112 G2 reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/365talents/reviews) , and individual reviews point to the same strengths.


One[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/365talents/reviews/365talents-review-12575361) writes, “The personalized learning recommendations help employees find relevant resources instantly. It removes noise from our learning catalog and supports upskilling paths.” Recurring themes in 365Talents reviews:


- User-friendly interface and skills mapping
- Internal mobility that matches people to roles and projects
- Personalized recommendations that cut catalog noise


Docebo’s enterprise proof shows up in named customer results.[Alstom](https://365talents.com/en/resources/case_studies/alstom-builds-a-global-skills-intelligence-platform-with-365talents/) deployed 365Talents inside a SAP SuccessFactors environment, and about nine months after launch it reported 55,000 active employees, 65% manager and employee engagement, and 4,000 internal mobility applications. Those figures reflect participation and application activity, not completed transfers or Docebo LMS results.


Hear it straight from the customer:


**Eightfold AI** sits in a different category, and its reviews reflect that. It earns[4.2 out of 5 across 225 G2 reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/eightfold-ai/reviews) and[4.0 out of 5 across 14 Capterra reviews](https://www.capterra.com/p/221474/Eightfoldai) (verified September 2026).


One[Gartner Peer Insights reviewer](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/product/eightfold-talent-intelligence-platform) writes, “The user interface is intuitive, and the search capabilities make it easier to identify relevant candidates from large talent pools. We have also seen improvements in recruiter productivity and collaboration across hiring teams.” Reviewers most often praise AI candidate matching, sourcing, and recruiter workflows, and the recurring critique is that reporting and analytics stay at summary-dashboard level.

For a direct side by side,[Gartner Peer Insights in the AI in Career Pathing market](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/ai-in-career-pathing/compare/docebo-365talents-vs-eightfold) places Docebo (365Talents) at 4.5 out of 5 and Eightfold at 4 out of 5, on small review counts that make the comparison directional.


## **Questions to ask during your platform demo**


- Show one employee’s skill record and label which skills are inferred versus validated, and by whom.
- Map a specialized job title into the framework, then correct a poor mapping live.
- Take an employee from a skill gap through assigned learning to a readiness review, and name every product involved.
- Demonstrate an internal opportunity application, and show applications separately from completed moves.
- Walk through the external recruiting workflow if hiring is in scope for your purchase.
- Show a compliance course record, including the content format and the renewal or recertification schedule.
- Demonstrate an HRIS update syncing through, then a failed sync, and name who owns the fix and the support path.


## **Here’s how to decide if you need Docebo or Eightfold AI**


There’s no single winner here, so match the decision to your primary problem.


If learning delivery is central to your mandate, shortlist Docebo for the LMS and add 365Talents when you need a governed skills and mobility layer connected to that delivery. This is the strongest case for the combined Docebo with 365Talents workflow, because gaps, learning, and readiness live in one loop.


If external hiring leads the purchase, shortlist Eightfold and weigh its recruiting and matching depth first.


If[internal mobility](https://www.docebo.com/solutions/internal-mobility/) is the main objective, evaluate both on one shared scenario: the same employee, the same role, and the same development path from gap to move. Compare adoption, application activity, and completed moves as distinct measures.


If Eightfold already supports your recruiting well, consider coexistence and test whether adding dedicated skills and learning products gives you a stronger development loop.


And if you only need basic training delivery, evaluate the LMS requirement on its own before adding a skills layer you’re not ready to act on.


When you’re ready to see the closed loop in action,[book a Docebo demo](https://www.docebo.com/demo/) focused on the journey from a role-level skill gap to learning delivery and a readiness review. To go deeper on the skills layer specifically, explore[skills intelligence](https://www.docebo.com/products/skills-intelligence/) .


## **FAQs**


### **Is Eightfold AI an LMS or a replacement for Docebo?**


Eightfold AI is a talent intelligence platform for acquisition and talent management, not a learning management system. It recommends development but doesn’t run and record courses the way an LMS does. Before you retire an existing LMS, test your compliance, certification, and multi-audience training requirements against what delivers and tracks the content.


### **Is 365Talents included with Docebo?**


No. 365Talents, a Docebo company, is sold as a separate product and[isn’t bundled into Docebo’s Elevate or Enterprise packaging](https://www.docebo.com/products/skills-intelligence/) . You can add it to a Docebo LMS subscription for the combined skills-to-learning workflow, or run it alongside a learning system you already own. Treat it as its own line item when you build your budget and total cost of ownership.


### **Can Docebo and Eightfold AI work together?**


They play complementary roles, so coexistence is an architectural option rather than a prebuilt, out-of-the-box connector. Eightfold can lead recruiting while Docebo handles learning delivery. If you plan to run both, confirm the specific integration approach, the data that moves between them, the refresh cadence, and who owns support when a sync fails.


### **Which is better for upskilling and internal mobility?**


It depends on your development workflow, so compare the whole path rather than a single feature. The deciding factors are how each platform validates skills and how it moves an employee from a recommendation to an actual assigned course and a completed move. Evaluate both on one shared scenario, and measure applications separately from completed transfers.


### **How do they handle SCORM, xAPI, and compliance training?**


Docebo LMS supports SCORM, xAPI, and AICC per the[Docebo Help Center training material documentation](https://help.docebo.com/hc/en-us/categories/36751714039058-Training-material) , and it manages compliance tracking, recurring certifications, and renewals. Eightfold isn’t a learning management system, so for any configuration you’re considering, ask which system runs the content and records completions. Confirm the content-standard support directly with each vendor for your specific programs.
